questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.

She will clear the test tomorrow.

options.text: The test would be cleared by her tomorrow.
The test should be cleared by her the previous day.
The test must be cleared by her the coming day.
The test will be cleared by her the next day.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is **'**The test will be cleared by her the next day'.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In the second part of the given sentence, the singular form of the verb will is correct.
 
• In the given sentence, the subject is '**she**' and the object is '**the test**'.
 
• In passive voice, the object comes first, followed by the form of '**be**' and the past participle of the main verb, and then the subject.
 
• Therefore, the correct sentence in the passive voice is: The test will be cleared by her the next day.

Hence, the correct answer is option 4.

Correct sentence: ***The test will be cleared by her the next day***.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Note that passive voice changes the focus of the sentence from the subject to the object.
 
• Passive voice is often used to highlight the action itself rather than the doer of the action.
 
• It is commonly used in formal and scientific writing to emphasize the action.

questions.question:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect speech.

He said, “I can speak three languages fluently.”

options.text: He said that he was able to speak three languages fluently.
He said that he will be able to speak three languages fluently.
He said that he can speak three languages fluently
He said that he could speak three languages fluently.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is 'He said that he could speak three languages fluently**'**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• When converting direct speech to indirect speech, the **present tense** of the verb often changes to the **past tense**.
 
• Here, the direct speech sentence uses "**can**," which changes to "**could**" in the indirect speech form.
 
• The reporting verb "**said**" remains the same when transforming the sentence.
 
• There is no change in the content of the sentence except for the verb tense.

Hence, the correct answer is option 4.

Correct sentence: ***He said that he could speak three languages fluently.***.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Indirect speech is used to report what someone has said without quoting them directly.
 
• It often requires changing the pronoun and the tense of the verb.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the word ‘incarcerate’.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is: **Liberate**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The word **"incarcerate"** means to imprison or confine someone. (कैद करना)

 
 
• **Example: **The government decided to **incarcerate **the criminal for his serious offenses.
 
 
 
• **"Liberate"** refers to the action of setting someone free from imprisonment, slavery, or oppression. (मुक्त करना)
 
 
• **Example: **The activists worked tirelessly to **liberate **the political prisoners.
 
 
 
• Hence, we can infer that the opposite of **'incarcerate'** is **'liberate'**.

Therefore, the correct answer is: **Option 3**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

Here are the other options explained along with their Hindi meanings and example sentences:

 
• **Invite** (आमंत्रित करना): To make a polite, formal, or friendly request to someone to go somewhere or to do something.

 
 
• **Example:** She decided to **invite **all her friends to the party.
 
 
 
• **Reject** (अस्वीकार करना): To dismiss as inadequate, unacceptable, or faulty.
 
 
• **Example:** He was sad to learn that the committee would **reject **his application.
 
 
 
• **Commit** (प्रतिबद्ध करना): To perpetrate or carry out (a mistake, crime, or immoral act).
 
 
• **Example:** She didn't expect him to **commit **such a serious error.
